hero.intro: DMP is a national manufacturer that sells through dealers, so every search measure here is national, in Semrush's US database, pulled on 9 November 2026. The backlink concentration figures and the brand reputation search come from the earlier pull of 13 September 2026 and are dated where they appear. The page-level numbers come from an audit of 241 public pages on www.dmp.com on 9 November 2026: the home page, the pages, the product categories and a sample of product pages. A correction to the September report: that crawl started at the redirecting apex and could read one URL, so its findings about the home page's title, H1, canonical, robots.txt, sitemap and structured data were wrong for the real site. They are replaced here. This is the baseline we measure against at 30, 60 and 90 days.
tiles: organic keywords in the US database, but 75 percent of the traffic is navigational
organic visits a month, worth $248,538 a month in paid equivalent
national category searches with DMP in the top ten, such as fire alarm control panel and access control panel
Authority Score, against 66 at honeywell.com, 52 at axis.com, 51 at avigilon.com and 44 at adiglobaldistribution.us
hero.heading: Where dmp.com stands, and what it is worth to fix

findings.fix: Give each product category a page written as the answer to the buyer's search (what it is, which listings and certifications apply, how it connects, which model fits), with question headings, FAQPage markup and links down to the products. In the build, starting with panels, access control, fire and communicators.
findings.cost: A dealer or specifier who does not yet know DMP and searches by category meets Honeywell, Axis, Avigilon, the distributors and the parts retailers instead. DMP's category pages exist, at /products/control-panels and /products/access-control, but they rank 22nd and 42nd.
findings.title: DMP is not in the top ten for any of the national category searches dealers and specifiers run
findings.evidence: Seven category searches were checked in Semrush's US database on 9 November 2026. DMP is not in the top ten for any of them. Its best positions are 22 for 'alarm panel' (1,300 a month, difficulty 20) and 42 for 'access control panel' (480 a month, difficulty 16). It has no top-100 position for 'fire alarm control panel' (5,400 a month, difficulty 24), 'wireless alarm system' (1,300, difficulty 46), 'commercial access control system' (720, difficulty 30) or 'security keypad' (320, difficulty 13), and sits at 35 for 'cellular alarm communicator' (70, difficulty 0). Who holds the top spots: buildings.honeywell.com at 1 for 'fire alarm control panel', adiglobaldistribution.us at 1 for 'access control panel', hanwhavision.com at 1 and avigilon.com at 2 for 'commercial access control system', alarmgrid.com at 1 for 'alarm panel' and for 'cellular alarm communicator'. Where DMP does win is its own cellular communicator page: 'cell communicator' (260 a month) at 3 and 'alarm system cellular communicator' (110) at 4.

findings.fix: Run the national question set against an assistant with web search before day 30 and record the answers and the sources read. Meanwhile build the category pages, FAQPage markup, Product markup and sameAs links that give an engine something to read and attribute. In the build, with the test in the first 30 days.
findings.cost: Until the test is run the honest position is that we do not know. What we do know is that the pages an assistant would be reading for these questions belong to other companies, and that dmp.com carries no Product, FAQPage or sameAs markup to help an engine attribute an answer to DMP.
findings.title: No test yet of whether AI assistants name DMP for national buyer questions
findings.evidence: The September local test is withdrawn because it measured local installers, not the dealers and specifiers DMP sells through. A national test has not been run yet. The questions we will put to an assistant with web search are the ones a dealer or specifier would ask: which manufacturers make a UL-listed commercial intrusion panel with cellular communication, which access control panel works with mobile credentials, which fire alarm control panel is listed for commercial use, which alarm communicators support dual-path reporting, and which manufacturers sell only through dealers. What is measured today is the sources an assistant would read: the top ten Google results for seven national category searches, listed in the AI answer section below, are led by buildings.honeywell.com, adiglobaldistribution.us, alarmgrid.com, avigilon.com and axis.com. dmp.com is in none of those top tens.

findings.title: The front door takes three hops, and robots.txt answers 404
findings.evidence: https://dmp.com/ answers 301 to http://www.dmp.com/, which then answers 307, a temporary redirect, rather than one permanent redirect to https. https://www.dmp.com/robots.txt returns HTTP 404 although the file holds rules and two Sitemap lines; crawlers treat a 4xx robots file as no file, so the rules and the sitemap declaration are never read. The XML sitemap itself is live at /sitemaps-1-sitemap.xml and lists 369 products, 26 categories and 197 pages, and a second Sitemap line points at a gforce.www.dmp.com host.
findings.cost: Search engines and AI crawlers that start at the apex or over http make extra hops, one of them temporary, and the file meant to steer them and declare the sitemap is ignored. DMP's crawl policy is whatever the 404 implies, not a decision.
findings.fix: Serve every address variant with one permanent 301 to https://www.dmp.com/, return robots.txt with a 200, declare the sitemap in it, name the AI crawlers and drop the gforce line. In the build, week one.

findings.title: Organization markup exists, but nothing describes the products, the questions or the profiles
findings.evidence: Of 241 pages audited, 226 carry Organization, WebPage and BreadcrumbList markup with the headquarters address, phone number and founding date. None carries Product, ItemList or FAQPage markup, none has a sameAs link, and none declares a contact point (0 of 241), although DMP publishes four support lines with hours. The most specific type on a product page is WebPage.
findings.cost: Search engines and answer engines know who DMP is, but not what the 369 products are, which questions they answer or which LinkedIn, YouTube and Crunchbase profiles belong to the company, so they fall back on Indeed, Glassdoor and Reddit for the brand and on distributors for the products.
findings.fix: Add Product markup from the product table to every product page, ItemList to the category pages, FAQPage and CollectionPage to the system pages, a ContactPoint for each support line, and sameAs links to LinkedIn, YouTube and Crunchbase. Keep the Springfield headquarters address in the Organization markup as it is. In the build.

Build the eight system pages and a resource hub that target category language rather than part numbers, starting with access control and fire. In the build for the pages, 90-day plan for the content programme.
findings.cost: The site harvests existing dealers and customers looking up model numbers and support logins. It does not introduce DMP to anyone who has not already heard the name, so the whole top of the funnel depends on trade shows, reps and word of mouth.
findings.title: Three quarters of the traffic is people who already know the brand
findings.evidence: Semrush's intent split for dmp.com on 9 November 2026 puts 17,705 of 23,660 monthly visits, 75 percent, in navigational searches. The top organic term is 'dmp' at 9,900 a month, bringing 7,920 visits, a third of all traffic on its own, followed by 'digital monitoring products' at 880 and a long list of part numbers and product names: 'dmp support' 590, 'dmp keypad' 480, 'dmp xr550' 260, 'dmp 734' 260. Non-navigational traffic is 5,955 visits a month. The one high-volume non-branded term among the leading pages is 'white on white paper' at 12,100 a month in the September pull, position 9, which lands on the JamAlert white paper and has nothing to do with security.

findings.title: The catalogue is built by part number, with no page written for the buyer's own search words
findings.evidence: dmp.com organises its catalogue by product category (26 categories) and by part number (369 product pages). No page is written for the phrase a buyer types. Semrush shows the top-ranking pages are individual SKUs and brand pages such as /products/control-panels/xr-series/xr550 and /products/access-control/modules/734, while the national category searches go to manufacturers, distributors and retailers: for 'access control systems' (9,900 a month) and 'fire detection and fire alarm system' (6,600) DMP held no position in the September pull, and 'alarm panel' goes to alarmgrid.com and alarmsystemstore.com.
findings.cost: A dealer or specifier who searches a category meets a part number page written for someone who already chose the part, so the searches go to manufacturers with category pages and to distributors.
findings.fix: Build a page for each system line (intrusion, access control, fire, video, communicators, wireless, panels and keypads, Virtual Keypad and software), each with question headings, FAQPage markup and links down to the products. In the build.
Publish an about and proof page carrying dealer testimonials, installation case studies and Review markup, and link it from the home page and every service page. In the 30-day plan.
findings.cost: Anyone checking DMP out before specifying it, and any AI answer summarising the brand, reads employment complaints first because the company publishes nothing that answers the question. No Review or AggregateRating markup exists anywhere on the site to compete.
findings.title: The brand reputation result is owned by job boards and Reddit
findings.evidence: The search 'digital monitoring products reviews', in the 13 September 2026 pull, returned indeed.com at 1, glassdoor.com at 2 and a Reddit thread at 3 titled 'I can't recommend anyone work for DMP'. Positions 4 to 10 were simplyhired.com, a second glassdoor.com result, facebook.com, a second indeed.com result, ipvm.com, mammothsecurity.com and securityinfowatch.com. dmp.com appeared nowhere on the page. Semrush returned no record for this phrase in the US database on 9 November, so it has not been re-measured.

findings.fix: Put six to eight questions with direct answers and FAQPage markup at the foot of each of the eight system pages, drawn from the question lists above. In the build for the markup, 30-day plan for the copy.
findings.cost: These are exactly the phrasings answer engines lift from, and DMP has no page shaped as an answer to any of them.
findings.title: Nothing on the site answers a question in the words buyers use
findings.evidence: Of 241 pages audited, 36 have a question heading and none carries FAQPage markup. Semrush records real question demand across the lines: 'how to turn off fire alarm system' 720 a month, 'how to reset fire alarm system' 320, 'what is access control system' 210, 'what is fire alarm system' 210, 'what is a central station fire alarm system' 170. Intrusion questions are thinner, so intrusion content should be written for dealers and specifiers. Whether competitors carry FAQPage markup was not measured in the national pull.

findings.title: Pages say little about what they are: short titles, one shared description, thin copy, images without alt text
findings.evidence: Of 241 pages audited, 66 have a title under 25 characters (usually the part name and 'DMP.com'), 107 share one default meta description, 175 have fewer than 300 words (median 174) and 226 have at least one image with no alt attribute. 137 use the same default Open Graph image. The home page is the strongest page at 52 of 100, and no page scores above a D. 15 pages returned an unusual response during the crawl (title 'POST data') and need a re-check, so they are left out of these counts.
findings.cost: A title like 'XT75 | DMP.com' does not say what the product is, so a search result or an AI summary cannot tell a panel from a keypad. Shared descriptions and thin copy give engines nothing to quote, and missing alt text is an accessibility failure on almost every page.
findings.fix: Generate a descriptive title, a unique description, alt text and 300 or more words from the product table for every product page, and give shared links a product image. In the build.
Point the control panel, access control, fire and communicator category pages at these terms and build supporting question pages beneath them. In the 90-day plan.
findings.cost: There is no pipeline of non-branded demand from dealers and specifiers, while terms DMP already ranks for in the teens and twenties sit on news articles and the wrong pages.
findings.title: The national category terms DMP could win are being left to distributors and manufacturers with category pages
findings.evidence: DMP's rankings for the B2B category terms are all outside the top ten: 'cloud based access control' (720 a month) at 14 on a news article, 'alarm panel' (1,300) at 22, 'door access control software' (170) at 23, 'cellular alarm communicator' (70) at 35, 'access control panel' (480) at 42. Several are within reach of an Authority Score of 39: difficulty is 16 for 'access control panel', 20 for 'alarm panel', 24 for 'fire alarm control panel', 30 for 'commercial access control system', and from the September pull 22 for 'door access control systems', 29 for 'access control companies' and 42 for 'fire detection and fire alarm system'. The consumer head terms (such as 'security camera' at 550,000 a month and 'home security systems' at 74,000) are at difficulty 46 to 79 and are not the target for a manufacturer that sells through dealers.

findings.fix: Earn links from domains that have none yet, starting with security trade publications, standards and industry associations, dealer sites and integrator partners, and ask partners who link with a logo to put the company name in the alt text. In the 90-day plan.
findings.cost: The headline link number overstates the real position. If that one relationship or that one site changes, most of the profile goes with it, and image links say nothing about what DMP makes, so they build no topical signal.
findings.title: The backlink total rests on one relationship
findings.evidence: On 13 September 2026 the profile was 22,880 links from 1,916 referring domains, with 88.1 percent of links passing authority; a Semrush bulk comparison on 9 November 2026 reads 19,236 backlinks from 3,724 referring domains. Authority Score is 39, level with alarmgrid.com at 39 and below adiglobaldistribution.us at 44, avigilon.com at 51, axis.com at 52 and honeywell.com at 66. In the September pull nationaljeweler.com accounted for 85.3 percent of every link to the site, and 89.7 percent of links, 20,514 of 22,880, were image links carrying no anchor text. The two pulls differ, so the concentration should be re-checked.

findings.fix: Publish a deliberate robots.txt that names and allows the eight crawlers, and an llms.txt listing the home page, the eight system pages and the support hub. In the build, week one.
findings.cost: Low today, but the moment anyone adds a default robots.txt the access can disappear without being noticed, and there is no file telling an engine which pages matter.
findings.title: AI crawlers are allowed by accident, not by policy, and llms.txt is not published
findings.evidence: GPTBot, ClaudeBot, anthropic-ai, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, CCBot, Bingbot and Googlebot are all able to read the site, which scores 94 of 100 on AI answer access against 100 at safehome.org. That permission exists because the robots file answers 404 and is ignored, not because a file grants it. llms.txt is not published (the address returns 404).

findings.fix: Once the category pages exist, run a small brand-defence campaign on the five brand terms and a test on 'access control companies' and 'door access control systems'. In the 90-day plan.
findings.cost: Nothing is being wasted, but nothing is being defended either. With 'dmp' at 9,900 a month, a competitor or a distributor can bid on the brand name at any time and pay very little for it.
findings.title: No paid search at all, and no paid-sourced contacts in the CRM
findings.evidence: DMP runs 0 ad keywords. HubSpot records 0 contacts from paid search, 0 from paid social and 0 from display in the 90 days since 15 June 2026. In Semrush's US database on 9 November 2026 adiglobaldistribution.us runs 55 ad keywords, axis.com 82 and avigilon.com 11.

compare.intro: Each column is Semrush US-database data for the root domain, pulled on 9 November 2026, with the positions taken from the live top ten for each search on the same day. The honeywell.com column covers all Honeywell business lines, not only security. These are the companies that hold the national category searches; competitors' page markup and word counts were not part of this pull.
compare.verdict: The pages that win the national category searches are category pages from manufacturers with many times DMP's referring domains, plus distributors and parts retailers. DMP already has category pages for panels and access control, but they rank 22nd and 42nd. Closing the gap means writing each category page as the answer a dealer or specifier is looking for, and earning links from dealers, integrators and trade media.

moves.title: Fix the front door: one 301, a working robots.txt, a declared sitemap
moves.body: https://dmp.com/ answers 301 to http://www.dmp.com/, which answers 307, and https://www.dmp.com/robots.txt returns HTTP 404 although it holds rules and Sitemap lines, so crawlers ignore it. Serve every address variant with a single permanent 301 to https://www.dmp.com/, return robots.txt with a 200 and declare the sitemap in it, name the eight AI crawlers so their access is a decision rather than an accident, publish llms.txt and remove the gforce line. This is the cheapest fix in the report and every other measurement depends on it.

moves.title: Describe the products, the questions and the profiles to machines
moves.body: Organization markup is already on 226 of 241 pages, with the Springfield headquarters address, phone number and founding date. Add what is missing: Product markup from the product table on every product page, ItemList on the category pages, FAQPage on the system pages, a ContactPoint for each of the four support lines and sameAs links to LinkedIn, YouTube and Crunchbase. This is what lets an engine say what DMP's 369 products are and attribute them to the company.

moves.title: Lift the national terms DMP already ranks for in the teens and twenties
moves.body: Several category terms already return a dmp.com page, but not the right one or not high enough: 'cloud based access control' (720 a month) at 14 on a news article, 'alarm panel' (1,300) at 22 on /products/control-panels, 'door access control software' (170) at 23, 'cellular alarm communicator' (70) at 35 and 'access control panel' (480) at 42 on /products/access-control. Rebuild those category pages so each answers its search in the opening paragraph, carries question headings and FAQPage markup, links to the models and spec sheets, and absorbs the news article's argument. DMP's cellular communicator page already holds positions 3 and 4 for 'cell communicator' and 'alarm system cellular communicator', and is the model for the rest.

DMP's catalogue is organised by category and part number, and no page is written for the buyer's phrase. Build one page for each system line (intrusion, access control, fire, video, communicators, wireless, panels and keypads, Virtual Keypad and software), each 900 words or more with question headings, FAQPage markup, links down to the matching products and an enquiry form. Use the measured question demand: 'how to turn off fire alarm system' 720 a month, 'how to reset fire alarm system' 320, 'what is access control system' 210, 'what is the best home video surveillance system' 210, and add the questions dealers and specifiers ask about listings, communicators and compatibility.
moves.title: Build the system pages with questions answered on them

moves.body: In the 13 September pull, 'digital monitoring products reviews' returned Indeed at 1, Glassdoor at 2 and a Reddit thread criticising DMP as an employer at 3, with dmp.com nowhere in the top ten, and 75 percent of organic traffic is navigational. Publish an about and proof page with dealer testimonials, case studies and Review markup, and link it from the home page and all eight system pages. At the same time point the access control and fire pages at the commercial terms within reach of an Authority Score of 39: 'access control companies' 1,600 a month at difficulty 29, 'door access control systems' 1,600 at 22, 'fire alarm control panel' 5,400 at 24. Support both with links from trade press, standards and industry bodies, integrators and dealer sites, since in the September pull 85.3 percent of the profile came from a single domain.
moves.title: Take back the brand result and start on the reachable commercial terms

do: Give the news, case studies and answer pages one index linked from the main navigation, and put Article markup on every post template.

Publish three answer pages tied to the pulled questions: what an access control system is and how it works, how a monitored fire alarm system works, and how to choose a video surveillance system. Each one answers the question in the first fifty words.
Add a FAQ block marked up as FAQPage to each of the eight system pages, using the pulled questions for that line, and link every post to its service line page.
Publish three more posts against the DIY wireless and smart smoke detector questions, and review the jamalert white paper page so the traffic it already earns lands on something relevant.
found: Publishing is news-led: press releases, personnel announcements, technical updates and case studies. None is written as an answer to a buyer's question.
Of 241 pages audited, 36 have a question heading and none has FAQPage markup, so very little on the site is shaped as an answer.

The question demand is real and unclaimed: "how to turn off fire alarm system" at 720 a month, "do it yourself wireless home security systems" at 320, "what is access control system" at 210, "what is the best home video surveillance system" at 210, and "how does access control system work" at 70.

Intrusion questions are thinner: "what is intrusion alarm system" is 20 a month and the rest of that set sits under 10, so intrusion content should be written for dealers and specifiers, not for search volume.
One resource page, /resources/white-papers/jamalert-white-paper, ranks 9th for "white on white paper" at 12,100 a month, which is accidental traffic from a phrase that has nothing to do with alarms.
blog.intro: dmp.com publishes news and updates, case studies, technical updates, spec sheets and white papers, but none is written as the answer to a buyer's question. Of 241 pages audited, 36 have a question heading and none carries FAQPage markup, and the median page has 174 words. That leaves nothing on the site written in the language a buyer or an AI engine uses when it asks how a system works, what it costs or which type to choose. Semrush does show a white paper URL ranking at position 9 for a 12,100 a month phrase, so long-form material exists, but it is not pointed at the questions people ask.
tiles: median words per page across the 241 audited pages
blog.heading: No blog, no insights section, no answers in buyers' words

do: Serve every address variant with one permanent 301 to https://www.dmp.com/, and give each page a title and description that name the product and the category.

Add Organization JSON-LD to the home page with the legal name, the headquarters address in Springfield, Missouri, the phone number, the logo and sameAs links to LinkedIn, Crunchbase, BBB, YouTube and Grokipedia.
Add Product markup from the product table to every product page, ItemList to the category pages, and FAQPage and CollectionPage to the system pages.
Complete the BBB, Crunchbase and LinkedIn entries so the details match the schema word for word, then add Review markup once first-party reviews are collected.
found: Organization markup is present on 226 of 241 pages audited, with the headquarters address, phone number and founding date. Product, ItemList and FAQPage markup are absent everywhere, and the most specific type on a product page is WebPage.
There are no sameAs links on any of the 241 pages, so nothing on dmp.com connects the company to its LinkedIn, Crunchbase, BBB or YouTube entries.
No page declares a contact point. DMP publishes four support lines with hours and email addresses, none of them in markup.
Titles are short, usually the part name and 'DMP.com' (66 of 241 are under 25 characters), and 107 pages share one default description.

Authority is not the main problem: Authority Score 39, level with alarmgrid.com and behind axis.com (52) and honeywell.com (66), on 3,724 referring domains in the 9 November comparison. The company is well linked and badly described.
entity.intro: An answer engine decides what a company is from structured data and from the profiles that data points to. DMP's pages already say who the company is, with the address, phone number and founding date in Organization markup. What they do not say is what the products are, which questions they answer, which profiles are the company's, or how to reach each support team. Every machine reading the site has to guess those.
tiles: pages with Product, FAQPage or ContactPoint markup
referring domains pointing at dmp.com, 9 November 2026
entity.heading: Nothing on dmp.com tells a machine who Digital Monitoring Products is

today: Semrush shows dmp.com with 7,521 organic keywords and 23,660 organic visits a month in the US database, valued at $248,538 a month in equivalent paid traffic, and zero paid keywords running (9 November 2026).
75 per cent of that organic traffic is navigational, 17,705 of 23,660 visits: "dmp" alone at 9,900 a month brings 7,920 of them, a third of the total.

The home page is sound on the basics: a title, one H1, a canonical tag, 628 words, a phone link, a form and Organization markup with the address, phone number and founding date. It still scores 52 of 100, and across 241 public pages the average is 35 and none scores above a D.

https://www.dmp.com/robots.txt answers HTTP 404 although it holds rules and Sitemap lines, so crawlers ignore it. The XML sitemap is live and lists 369 products, 26 categories and 197 pages. The apex takes a 301 to http://www.dmp.com/, then a 307.

The pages that earn the visits are product and support pages: the home page takes 49.01 per cent of organic traffic across 209 keywords, the dealer admin page 3.52 per cent, the 734 access module page 2.93 per cent and the control panels index 2.63 per cent (13 September pull).

175 of 241 pages have fewer than 300 words, 107 share one default meta description, 66 titles are under 25 characters, 226 pages have an image without alt text, and none carries Product, FAQPage or sameAs markup.

For seven national category searches DMP is not in the top ten for any. The best positions are 'alarm panel' at 22 and 'access control panel' at 42; its cellular communicator page holds 3 and 4 for 'cell communicator' and 'alarm system cellular communicator'.

Backlinks: Authority Score 39 on 3,724 referring domains (9 November). In the 13 September pull, 85.3 per cent of the links came from a single domain, nationaljeweler.com, and 89.7 per cent were image links carrying no anchor text.

Semrush US database. honeywell.com covers all Honeywell business lines.

aeo.intro: An assistant test on national buyer questions has not been run yet, and the September local test is withdrawn. What follows is the top ten of Google results for seven national category searches, from Semrush's US database on 9 November 2026, because those are the pages an assistant with web search reads first. dmp.com is in none of them. The questions we will put to an assistant, such as which manufacturers make a UL-listed commercial intrusion panel with cellular communication, are listed in the findings and will be run and recorded before day 30.

backlinks.heading: 3,724 referring domains by the 9 November comparison, and in September 85 per cent of the links came from one site

local: Brand reputation search, 13 September 2026 pull: 'digital monitoring products reviews' returned no dmp.com page in the top ten. Semrush had no record for this phrase in the US database on 9 November, so it has not been re-measured.
Indeed held first place with "Working at Digital Monitoring Products, Inc.: 25 Reviews", an employer review page, not a product one.
Glassdoor held second place and appeared twice in the top ten with employer reviews.
A Reddit thread sat third, titled "I can't recommend anyone work for DMP".
SimplyHired, Facebook and a second Indeed listing took four more of the ten places.
The only industry results were ipvm.com, mammothsecurity.com and securityinfowatch.com, none of them owned or influenced by DMP.
No star rating appeared in any result title except Indeed's count of 25 reviews, and no review markup was found on dmp.com, so no rating can be shown next to the brand in search.

Across seven national category searches on 9 November 2026 the top tens are held by manufacturers (Honeywell, Axis, Avigilon, Hanwha Vision), distributors (ADI Global Distribution) and parts retailers (Alarm Grid, Alarm System Store); DMP is in none.
plan: Fix the front door. Serve every address variant with one permanent 301 to https://www.dmp.com/, return robots.txt with a 200 and declare the sitemap in it, name the AI crawlers, publish llms.txt, and give every page its own title and description. Run the first national assistant test.

Build the eight system pages: intrusion, access control, fire, video, communicators and monitoring, wireless, panels and keypads, and Virtual Keypad and software. Each gets 800 words or more, H2 sections, a FAQ block marked up as FAQPage using the pulled questions, Service schema, ten or more internal links and an enquiry form.

Build the about and proof pages, add sameAs links from the home page schema to LinkedIn, Crunchbase, BBB, YouTube and Grokipedia, and add Product markup to the catalogue pages. Keep the Springfield headquarters address in the Organization markup.

Take back the brand result: publish an about page, a careers page and a company news page under dmp.com so branded queries have owned destinations, start collecting first-party reviews, and publish the first three answer posts against the access control, fire alarm and video surveillance questions.

Re-run the same seven national category searches, the same assistant questions and the same page audit against this baseline, and decide whether to open a small paid search test on the reachable access control terms.

hub.heading: Where you stand in search today, and what changes
hub.intro: Measured before we touched anything, so the work can be judged against it.
today: Semrush shows dmp.com with 7,521 organic keywords and 23,660 organic visits a month in the US database, valued at $248,538 a month in equivalent paid traffic, and zero paid keywords running.

75 per cent of that organic traffic is navigational: "dmp" alone at 9,900 a month brings a third of it. For seven national category searches, such as fire alarm control panel and access control panel, DMP is not in the top ten.

The home page is sound on the basics (title, one H1, canonical, 628 words, a phone link, a form and Organization markup) and still scores 52 of 100. Across 241 public pages the average is 35 and none scores above a D.
https://www.dmp.com/robots.txt answers HTTP 404 although it holds rules and Sitemap lines, so crawlers ignore it. The sitemap is live, and the apex takes a 301 to http://www.dmp.com/ and then a 307.

The pages that earn the visits are product and support pages: the home page takes 49.01 per cent of organic traffic across 209 keywords, the dealer admin page 3.52 per cent, the 734 access module page 2.93 per cent and the control panels index 2.63 per cent.
No page carries Product, FAQPage, ContactPoint or sameAs markup. 175 of 241 pages have fewer than 300 words and 107 share one default description.
after: Every URL answers once, at one canonical host, with a working robots.txt and a declared sitemap.
Eight system pages, each with question headings and a FAQ marked up as FAQPage.
Product, ItemList and ContactPoint markup, with sameAs links to the company's profiles and the headquarters address in the Organization markup.
Category pages for panels, access control, fire and communicators written as the answer to the dealer's or specifier's search.
A title, description, alt text and real copy on every product page, generated from the product table.
keep: One permanent hop instead of a 301 and then a 307
Product pages that already earn traffic keep their address, lowercase
hub.note: Rankings and traffic depend on the market and on what you publish after launch. What we promise is that nothing about the build is the reason they do not come, that every number is re-measured at 30, 60 and 90 days, and that you see the same report we do.
